=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- Requirement: "Failure escalations under CLAUDE.md §28.C no longer wait for a human." The PR description states that the stop now posts `<!-- ai:claude-blocked:v1 kind=escalation stop=<stop id> -->` (on the source issue in issue mode, otherwise on the final PR) and hands its project checker an `escalation` wait. The checker starts the judge (Opus 5.5, high effort) about two minutes later. Only the human-only stops (Q8) and the start-up checks wait for a person. A blocked stage sends no `PushNotification` for an escalation stop; the judge sends exactly one for `close`, and exactly one when it ends at `Status: BLOCKED` without a choice.
  Expected change site: `README.md`, lines 1333-1337 (Claude issue failure modes paragraph).
  Evidence of absence: The README still says, verbatim: "A Claude session that must stop (CLAUDE.md §28.C: an exhausted cap, a failed security or validation run, an ask-first operation, a missing base branch) comments once on the issue, labels it `ai:claude-blocked`, and sends a push notification; answer there and comment `/reclarify` to resume." Two of those four cases (an exhausted cap, a failed security or validation run) are now escalation stops that go to the judge without a `PushNotification` and without waiting for a human `/reclarify`. The PR diff updates `CLAUDE.md §28.C` (lines 2259-2279) and `CLAUDE.md §28.G` (the new section) to the new contract, and updates `agents.md` (lines 893-957 and 1012-1024) for the same change, but the README's failure-modes paragraph is unchanged. `agents.md` §3 of the contributing rules in `CLAUDE.md` (`§7 (update README.md / agents.md on behavior change)`) names the README as the surface for behavior changes. No diff hunk in `README.md` adjusts the contradiction; the consumers who onboard via the README are told the old, contradicting failure mode.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- Requirement: "Failure escalations under CLAUDE.md §28.C no longer wait for a human" (PR description, top of "What changes"). The PR changes CLAUDE.md §28.C so that escalation stops (exhausted caps, failed security/validation runs, terminal validation classes, blocked follow-ups, FIX-DEFECTIVE) hand the checker the escalation wait instead of notifying and waiting for /reclarify. Only human-only stops (ask-first operations, no claude-code-remote tools, depth-limit refusal) still notify and wait.
  Expected change site: README.md, lines 1333-1337 (the "Claude issue failure modes" paragraph).
  Evidence of absence: README.md lines 1333-1337 still say "A Claude session that must stop (CLAUDE.md §28.C: an exhausted cap, a failed security or validation run, an ask-first operation, a missing base branch) comments once on the issue, labels it ai:claude-blocked, and sends a push notification; answer there and comment /reclarify to resume." This lumps together escalation stops (which no longer notify or wait) with human-only stops (which still do). Two of the four cases the README lists — "an exhausted cap" and "a failed security or validation run" — now go to the escalation judge without a push notification. The PR's Files table does not include README.md, and no diff hunk updates this passage. An operator reading the README would believe they must answer every ai:claude-blocked stop by hand, when in fact the judge handles most of them.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
